A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCR study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the revised proofs and v3's additional experiment and checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-model LLM experiments in Section 2 and Table 1, plus transformer training experiments and analyses in Section 3.2 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds PopQA-OCR experiments with five LLMs in Appendix D and Table 2.

M1.justification: The factorized and non-factorized one-layer linear-attention models, prediction functions, cross-entropy objectives, and training framework remain unchanged. The revised theoretical assumptions do not introduce a new model component or algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 retains the synthetic association settings and symbolic OCR task, adding PopQA-OCR: a controlled birthplace–sport QA scenario with real names and randomly paired associations. This extends population and input-format coverage within the existing OCR task.

E2.justification: The evaluated LLM set remains Gemma-2-9B, OLMo-7B, Qwen-2-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Llama-3-8B, including the new PopQA comparison. The factorized/non-factorized model and nuclear/Frobenius SVM comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The added PopQA-OCR protocol uses 500 subjects, 10 association pairs, and a 0.5 training ratio; the retained synthetic setup uses 100 subjects, five pairs, and 0.2. The LLM batch description changes from 256 to full batch, while 100 epochs and the learning-rate sweep remain. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The architecture comparison, training curves, weight inspection, SVM geometry, and intrinsic-dimension sweep are retained. Appendix D adds benchmark performance without a separate new ablation, sensitivity test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 standard errors across three random-seed runs and Figure 7 standard-deviation shading across three seeds. The new PopQA table follows the same three-run standard-error convention; no new statistical procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained empirical figures preserve their reported findings. New Table 2 adds PopQA-OCR mean ranks of 0.68, 1.41, 3.30, 1.36, and 2.29 for Gemma, OLMo, Qwen, Mistral, and Llama respectively. These are additional-condition results, not matched-setting gains. Llama's entry is printed as 2.29 (4.26), with parentheses labeled standard errors.

T1.justification: v3 makes the factorized OCR and uniqueness guarantees conditional on new Assumption 3 and replaces the simultaneous-polarization uniqueness argument with new Lemmas 7–8. It also corrects Lemma 6's optimizer cases and lower-bound derivations, singular-value multiplicities, and the Frobenius-norm minimum. Appendix Theorem 6 is revised to match the main theorem's universal implication-margin statement. These substantially revise assumptions and mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same headline claims: OCR underlies both generalization and hallucination, factorization enables symbolic OCR, and implicit bias explains the distinction. The added evidence and conditional theorem do not produce corresponding changes to those headline formulations.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explains that real subject names can conflict with pretrained knowledge and interprets the QA results as continued OCR-driven hallucination. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations concerning one-layer theory and trainable key-query analysis remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds the authors' OCR-Theory code-release link, whereas v1 links only to the implementation it builds upon. It separately specifies one A100 GPU for one-layer experiments and four A100s for LLM experiments, and documents construction of PopQA-OCR. These improve disclosed reproducibility information without establishing that hardware usage changed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds connections to Abbe et al. on OOD generalization and several matrix-factorization implicit-bias studies, including Gunasekar et al. and Arora et al. v3 also cites Mallen et al. for PopQA. The existing OCR and transformer research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order remain intact. v3 makes local wording, heading, and proof-roadmap edits, inserts the real-data appendix, moves implementation details from D to E, and adds acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist. The overall scientific narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 adopts NeurIPS typesetting throughout, changing fonts, title and author arrangement, text density, equation wrapping, and figure/table placement. It adds PopQA Table 2 and renumbers the retained relation table as Table 3. This is broad visual reformatting, although the existing empirical graphics are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects identifiable mathematical inconsistencies and makes the uniqueness argument's additional assumption explicit, while improving code-access and compute documentation. PopQA-OCR adds limited corroboration under controlled real-entity QA conditions. The net gain is modest: the OCR guarantee is now conditional, headline claims remain broad, and Table 2's Llama mean of 2.29 with a stated standard error of 4.26 requires clarification.
